findings.F1: The book failed on its mean daily return, 0.028 % against the 0.05 % required, and on its Calmar, 0.445 against 0.75, with a deepest fall of 21.9 %; it earns only on Mondays (+0.135 % a day) and Tuesdays (+0.075 %) and is flat on the other five days (−0.015 % to +0.011 %), so its yearly return is spread thin while its falls come from a few large Monday bets.
findings.F2: The effect sits only in the most turbulent weekends: in the top fifth of the weekend-to-prior-week volatility ratio the unusual move is +1.38 % per case (t 3.14, 446 cases, strength 0.197, book +0.92 % per case), while the bottom two fifths show −0.19 % and −0.35 % (t −0.66, −1.05) and the middle fifths +0.10 % and +0.32 %.
findings.F3: The forecast is driven by the size of the weekend return more than by the volatility ratio (Spearman 0.92 with the weekend return scaled by the prior week's volatility, 0.56 with the ratio), so it places large positions where the idea fails: weekends with a large scaled return and a low or middle volatility ratio carry mean allocations of 0.41 and 0.50 and lose −0.45 % (t −0.73, 103 cases) and −0.76 % (t −1.65, 221 cases) per case.
findings.F4: By the size of the weekend return alone, the largest fifth has an unusual move of −0.47 % (t −1.07) while the second and third fifths show +0.65 % (t 2.07) and +0.56 % (t 1.87), so the cases the forecast sizes largest are, on average, the ones that turn against the book.
findings.F5: The worst tenth of cases loses −3.99 % of the book per case at a mean allocation of 0.64, and the best tenth gains +6.23 % at 0.69, with nearly the same volatility ratio (1.08 against 1.12) and scaled weekend return (1.13 against 1.17), so the falls come from heavily sized large-move weekends whose outcome the forecast cannot separate.
findings.F6: The continuation comes from falling weekends: cases following a falling weekend have an unusual move of +0.55 % (t 2.32, 1023 cases), and cases following a rising weekend have −0.002 % (t −0.01, 1205 cases).
findings.F7: The move is spread over both days, +0.16 % on day 1 (t 1.36) and +0.11 % on day 2 (t 1.13), and nothing follows on days 3 to 4 (−0.03 %, t −0.20), so holding longer would not add gain.

ideas.idea: When a coin's hourly moves over the weekend (Saturday 00:00 to Monday 00:00 UTC) were more volatile than over its previous week, the coin keeps moving in the direction of its weekend return over the next 2 days, and the continuation is larger the higher the weekend's volatility compared with the previous week, whatever the size of the weekend return itself.
ideas.consequence: A trader following turbulent weekends should scale the bet by how much more turbulent the weekend was than the week before, not by how far the price moved over the weekend.
ideas.name: volatility ratio drives continuation

ideas.idea: When a coin's hourly moves over the weekend (Saturday 00:00 to Monday 00:00 UTC) were more volatile than over its previous week, the coin keeps moving in the direction of its weekend return over the next 2 days, only after a falling weekend, and the further fall is larger the higher the weekend's volatility compared with the previous week.
ideas.consequence: A trader should follow turbulent weekend drops into Monday and Tuesday, more so the more turbulent the weekend, and refuse to chase turbulent weekend rallies.
ideas.name: turbulent weekend drops continue

ideas.idea: When a coin's weekend (Saturday 00:00 to Monday 00:00 UTC) return is large relative to its previous week's hourly volatility while its weekend hourly moves were no more volatile than that week's, the coin moves against its weekend return over the next 2 days, more so the larger the weekend return relative to the previous week's volatility.
ideas.consequence: A trader should refuse to follow, and may fade, a large weekend move made on calm hourly trading.
ideas.name: calm large weekend moves reverse
